Apple's annual September event is just weeks away, but according to multiple reports, one major product will be missing: the iPhone 18 base model. Here's its expected release date.

iPhone 18 base model delayed to early 2027, as Apple adjusts its new phone launch schedule

The iPhone launch event is Apple's most important product event of the year. Investors would be deeply concerned if the company failed to release its flagship new phones on schedule. This is one reason Apple has always stuck to a fixed iPhone launch rhythm.

Except for 2020, the event has been held in early September every year, typically unveiling a base model, two Pro models, and a fourth model — such as the iPhone Air.

However, according to numerous reports dating back to May 2025, the base model iPhone 18 will not be revealed next month.

This comes as a surprise, but by now there are so many corroborating sources that it would actually be more surprising if the base iPhone 18 did launch on schedule.

Why is the iPhone 18 missing from this year's September event?

The exact reason is unknown, but possible factors include:

  • Apple is deliberately spacing out iPhone launches to accommodate more new models, such as this year's iPhone Ultra.
  • Expected memory chip supply tightness has pushed Apple to adjust its plans to avoid severe shortages.

Regardless of the reason, the iPhone 18's absence from next month's event does not mean the model has been cancelled. The base iPhone 18 will still arrive — just pushed back to early 2027.

According to rumours, three new phones will be unveiled next month: the iPhone 18 Pro, iPhone 18 Pro Max, and iPhone Ultra.

Then in early 2027, another three models will follow: the iPhone 18, iPhone 18e, and iPhone Air 2.

That means they will appear by March at the latest. For reference, the iPhone 16e went on sale in February, and the iPhone 17e launched in March.

So if you want to get your hands on the new generation iPhone but aren't willing to pay the premium for the Pro or Ultra models, you'll have to wait a few more months.

What do you think about Apple's rumoured adjustment to the iPhone launch schedule? Feel free to share in the comments section.
